children.text: The Student App and Faculty Dashboard are connected through classroom activity. Faculty members manage learning tasks. Students receive the student-facing side of those tasks.
When faculty create an assignment for a class, eligible students can see it in their assignment experience.
When a student submits an assignment, faculty can review and grade it from their side.
When faculty grade an assignment, the student can receive a notification and view the grade and feedback tied to their own submission.
When faculty mark attendance, the student's attendance view updates for the relevant class session.
When faculty create or publish exams, quizzes, internal tests, or learning resources, students see what applies to their own class or academic group.
When faculty provide feedback or results, students receive the outcome without seeing faculty control panels.

This creates instant academic alignment. Faculty do the teaching work; students see the learning impact. The boundary remains clear. A student can submit, attempt, view, appeal, and respond. A faculty member can create, mark, grade, approve, publish, and manage classroom workflows.

Yes. Classgrid is designed for a student mobile experience on iOS and Android, with the same student identity and campus context as the desktop app. The mobile experience is built around speed. Students should be able to check what matters in seconds: today's class, pending assignment, new notification, fee reminder, exam update, message, or result. The student desktop sidebar and mobile navigation are intentionally simple.
The desktop sidebar gives students a focused navigation structure instead of a crowded administrative menu.
Core:
Home, Work, and Schedule.
Connect:
Messages, Notifications, and Forum.
Tools:
Classgrid AI, Virtual ID, and Marketplace.
Institution links:
My Requests, What's New, Organization, and Platform Feedback.
User menu:
Profile, Settings, Help and Support, and Log out.
The sidebar keeps the student out of administrative complexity while preserving access to everything they need.

The Work Page is the student's module grid. Instead of filling the sidebar with every academic feature, Classgrid places the complete student module set inside Work. This keeps navigation clean and gives students one familiar launchpad for academic tasks. The Work Page includes the student's available modules such as My Class, Assignments, Attendance, Results, Quizzes, Library, Fees, Hostel, Canteen, Notes Marketplace, Profile, and more.
The student mobile bottom navigation is designed around the five actions students repeat most often.
Home:
the student's academic starting point.
Work:
the module grid for assignments, attendance, exams, fees, library, and student tools.
Schedule:
timetable, academic calendar, holidays, and time-sensitive academic planning.
Messages:
communication with faculty, institution, and class channels where enabled.
Settings:
profile, preferences, support, and account controls.
The mobile experience is designed to handle real student conditions: inconsistent networks, low bandwidth, long days on campus, and repeated use.
Offline handling:
when the network is unavailable, the app can show a connection-aware screen and allow the student to retry instead of failing silently.
File uploads:
students can attach files where the workflow allows submissions or supporting documents.
Push-ready notifications:
the mobile experience supports device notification flows so important academic updates can reach students quickly when enabled by the institution.
Dark mode:
the interface supports light and dark themes, giving students a more comfortable experience across different environments.
The student mobile app is not a reduced version of Classgrid. It is the daily version.

Student login in Classgrid is designed to prevent duplicate identity, protect accounts, and keep sessions secure. The student's email is used for sign-in. Academic identifiers such as PRN, roll number, division, batch, or institution-issued student identity are used to keep the academic profile accurate and prevent duplicate student records inside the institution. This separation matters.
Email identifies the login:
it helps the student access the account securely.
PRN or roll number identifies the academic record:
it connects the student to the correct institution, class, division, course, or batch.
Duplicate prevention:
colleges can prevent repeated PRN usage, while schools can prevent repeated roll numbers inside the same division.
Correct portal access:
a student signs in through the student experience, while faculty and administrators use their own role-specific access.
After login, Classgrid uses secure session cookies to keep the student signed in.
The session cookie is used for authentication and account security.
It is protected so browser scripts cannot casually read it.
It is configured differently for secure production environments and local testing environments.
Mobile app sessions can remain active longer so students are not forced to sign in repeatedly during normal use.
New or unfamiliar devices may require extra verification before access is trusted.

Classgrid does not use student session cookies for third-party advertising or cross-site tracking. The purpose of login is simple: confirm the student, connect the right academic identity, and protect the student's private campus space.

PRN and Roll No are both student identifiers, but they are used for different academic purposes. PRN means Permanent Registration Number. In Classgrid, it is treated as a stronger college-style academic identity. It is especially important for junior colleges, degree colleges, and engineering institutions where the student may move across semesters, batches, branches, exams, fee records, results, certificates, and compliance workflows. Roll No is usually a class-level or division-level identity. It is especially useful in school environments, where students are organized by standard, section, division, and daily attendance groups.
PRN is long-term:
it helps identify a student across the broader academic journey inside the institution.
Roll No is class-specific:
it helps identify a student inside a particular class, section, or division.
PRN helps colleges avoid duplicate academic identities:
the same student should not be enrolled twice under the same official registration identity.
Roll No helps schools avoid duplicate classroom identities:
the same roll number should not repeat inside the same division.
Email is still the login identity:
students sign in with the registered email, while PRN or Roll No connects that login to the correct academic record.
In simple terms: email opens the account, PRN identifies the college student, and Roll No identifies the school student inside their class or division.

Usually, a coaching student does not need a PRN or a school-style Roll No. In Classgrid, coaching students are normally identified by their registered email and placed into the correct course, batch, or test-preparation group by the institute.
Email is used for login:
the coaching student signs in with the registered student email.
Course and batch define the academic identity:
the coaching institute places the student into the correct course, batch, or preparation track.
PRN is not the default coaching identity:
PRN is mainly useful for college, junior college, engineering, diploma, and compliance-heavy academic journeys.
Roll No is not the default coaching identity:
Roll No is mainly useful for school-style class and division management.
Custom institute IDs can still exist:
a coaching institute may use its own local student code or admission number, but Classgrid does not treat that as the same thing as PRN or school Roll No.
In simple terms: a school student usually has a Roll No, a college or engineering student usually has a PRN, and a coaching student is usually organized by course and batch.

Browser login is used when a student signs in from a desktop browser, laptop browser, tablet browser, or mobile browser. The student enters the registered email and password through the student login experience. Classgrid checks that the account belongs to a student, confirms that the student account is active, and then opens the correct student workspace.
Role-aware access:
a student is sent to the student experience, not to faculty or administrator dashboards.
Secure browser session:
the browser receives a protected session cookie so the student does not need to sign in again on every page.
Device protection:
unfamiliar devices may require extra verification before the session is trusted.
Clean logout:
when the student logs out, the session is cleared so the browser no longer has student access.
Browser login is ideal for longer study sessions, assignment uploads, exam preparation, profile completion, and desktop use in labs or at home.

App login is used when a student signs in through the Classgrid mobile app experience on iOS or Android. The student still uses the same verified student identity. The difference is that the app is optimized for daily use, faster return visits, mobile notifications, file uploads, dark mode, and connection-aware behavior.
Same student account:
browser and app login connect to the same student profile, classes, assignments, attendance, fees, library activity, and results.
Longer mobile continuity:
mobile app sessions can remain active longer so students are not forced to sign in repeatedly during normal campus use.
Mobile notifications:
the app can support student-facing alerts for grading, attendance, exams, messages, and institutional updates where enabled.
Offline awareness:
if the network drops, the app can show a retry-focused connection screen instead of leaving the student confused.

App login is best for the daily rhythm of campus life: checking the schedule, seeing notifications, submitting quick updates, reading messages, viewing attendance, and tracking academic progress on the move.
A student has 23 modules in the Work Page. These modules form the student's complete academic and campus workspace.

My Class gives the student a direct view of their academic group, classmates, classroom context, subjects, and class-related activity available to them. It is the student's anchor inside the institution.

Assignments let students view work assigned by faculty, understand what is due, submit their own response, and later review grades or feedback when faculty complete evaluation. Students submit their own work only. They cannot grade, create, or edit assignments for the class.

Internal Test helps students follow internal assessments, class tests, and academic evaluation activity published by faculty or examination teams. It gives students a clear place to track internal academic checkpoints.

Academic Planning gives students visibility into the institution's planned academic flow. This can include learning structure, semester planning, preparation windows, and academic milestones made available by the institution.
Curriculum helps students understand what they are expected to study. It connects students to the official learning structure shared by the organization, department, or course.

Certificate gives students access to digital certificates issued or managed through Classgrid. Students can view certificates that belong to them, while issuing and administrative controls remain with authorized staff.
Attendance lets students view their own attendance summary, session details, trends, and alerts. Students can understand their standing without waiting for manual communication from the department.
Leave lets students apply for leave or view leave-related activity where the institution enables that workflow. Approval and policy controls remain with authorized faculty or administrative staff.
Events shows campus activities, seminars, academic events, celebrations, or institutional programs relevant to the student. It helps students stay connected to campus life beyond daily classes.
Result gives students access to their own published academic outcomes. Students can view released marks, grades, or result summaries without accessing examination management controls.

Feedback gives students a structured way to share input with the institution. It can support course feedback, campus experience feedback, faculty feedback, or service feedback depending on institutional configuration.
Timetable shows the student's class schedule. For students in complex programs, this helps coordinate lectures, labs, practicals, exams, and academic planning.

Examination gives students access to exam-related activity such as schedules, assigned online exams, hall ticket updates, and results when published. Students participate in the exam experience but cannot manage examination operations.

Quizzes help students practice, attempt short assessments, and receive results when the institution releases them. This is especially useful for coaching, internal revision, and topic-level preparation.
Holidays shows institution-approved breaks and non-working days. It helps students plan assignments, exam preparation, travel, and attendance expectations.

Classgrid AI gives students an AI-powered study assistant experience where enabled. It can help students understand learning material, summarize notes, prepare questions, and study more efficiently while staying inside the Classgrid environment.

Hostel gives resident students access to hostel-related information such as allocation, mess updates, complaint status, and residence service communication where enabled. Students can view their own hostel context but cannot manage hostel operations.

Library gives students access to catalog discovery, issued books, reservations, return status, overdue alerts, and library activity connected to their own account. It reduces manual dependency on the library desk for routine tracking.
Fees lets students view their own dues, payments, receipts, and fee status. Where online payments are enabled by the institution, students can complete payment from the student experience.

Canteen gives students access to campus food service workflows where enabled. Students can interact with the canteen experience as consumers, while menu management and operational controls remain with authorized staff.

Notes Marketplace helps students access, share, and discover approved study material. The institution can keep quality control through review and verification workflows, while students benefit from a more organized study resource ecosystem.

Alumni connects students to post-study engagement, alumni updates, and placement-oriented opportunities where the institution enables those workflows. For final-year students, it can support the transition from campus life to professional life.

Profile gives students access to their own identity, onboarding status, personal information, academic details, documents, family information, address details, and preferences where editable by the student. Official academic identity remains controlled by the institution.

No. A student cannot independently delete their official institutional account from inside the student app. This is intentional. A student account is not only a login. It is connected to academic records, attendance, fees, exams, library transactions, certificates, institutional communication, compliance requirements, and historical campus activity. New students are added through authorized institution workflows.
Admission Department:
students can be added after admission and enrollment are completed.
Org Admin:
authorized organization administrators can add or import students for the institution.
Verified identity:
academic identifiers such as PRN or roll number help prevent duplicate student creation.
Onboarding:
students can complete their personal profile, family information, academic history, documents, and verification steps after their account is created.

Deletion requests are handled according to institutional data retention policies. This protects the student, the institution, and the integrity of academic records. Even when access changes, official records may need to be retained for legal, academic, financial, audit, or compliance reasons.
Classgrid is more than a digital notice board. It gives students premium campus capabilities that help them study, participate, resolve problems, and prepare for life beyond the classroom.

Classgrid AI helps students study more intelligently inside the academic environment. Where enabled, it can help summarize study material, explain topics, generate practice questions, support revision, and turn academic content into more useful learning assistance. Students benefit from AI without leaving the campus system or mixing study material across unrelated consumer apps.

Notes Marketplace gives students a structured place to access and share study materials. Students can discover notes connected to their organization and learning context, while review and verification workflows help preserve quality. For coaching and higher education environments, this creates a more serious learning resource layer than informal file sharing.

The Virtual ID Card gives students a digital campus identity. It can support scannable access patterns such as campus entry, identity verification, library use, events, or institution-specific checkpoints where the organization enables those flows. The value is simple: the student's verified identity becomes accessible inside the same app used for academics.

Classgrid gives students a way to raise issues without visiting administrative offices for every problem. Students can create support requests, describe the issue, and follow the status of the request where the institution has enabled student-facing support workflows. This is useful for campus services, account help, academic issues, fee questions, hostel concerns, library problems, or general support.

Classgrid can make academic achievement visible through certificates and progress-based recognition. Students can receive certificates for eligible activities, tests, events, courses, or institution-defined achievements. Certificates help turn learning milestones into portable academic proof.

Alumni and placement workflows help students move from campus learning to career readiness. Students can follow placement-related updates, alumni engagement, campus drives, and transition opportunities where the institution enables them. For engineering and higher education students, this helps Classgrid remain useful beyond the classroom and into the next stage of growth.
The Faculty App and Student App are connected, but they are not the same experience. Faculty members manage learning activity. Students participate in it and track the results.

answer.en: No, not by default. Teachers access their assigned teaching workflows. Admin dashboards, fee controls, payroll, institution settings, and organization-level reports remain with authorized administrators.

question.en: Can teachers access admin dashboards?

answer.en: Yes. Teachers can record attendance for assigned classes or sessions, depending on how the institution has configured attendance. Students can view their own attendance after it is recorded.

question.en: Can teachers mark attendance?

answer.en: Yes. Teachers can review submissions, assign grades, and send feedback for work connected to their assigned classes.

question.en: Can teachers grade assignments?

answer.en: Yes, where the institution enables the Online Exam Builder and gives the teacher authority to use it. Official result publication remains controlled by the institution's exam workflow.

question.en: Can teachers create online exams?

answer.en: Yes, where classroom join requests are enabled. This helps teachers control who gets access to a classroom or learning group.

question.en: Can teachers approve student join requests?

answer.en: Yes, where enabled. Teachers can access, recommend, share, or participate in structured study material workflows depending on the institution's rules.

question.en: Can teachers use the Notes Marketplace?

answer.en: Yes, where Go Live is enabled. Teachers can use live sessions for online classes, revision, doubt clearing, guest sessions, or hybrid learning.

question.en: Can teachers conduct live classes?

answer.en: No. Classgrid AI supports teaching and study workflows, but teachers remain responsible for instruction, judgment, feedback, and evaluation.

children.text: Teach, Evaluate, and Guide Every Class from One Workspace.

Classgrid gives teachers, faculty members, lecturers, professors, mentors, and tutors a focused digital workspace for daily academic work. It brings classes, students, attendance, assignments, quizzes, tests, timetable, notes, grading, feedback, live teaching, and communication into one clean experience. The goal is simple: teachers should spend less time chasing records and more time teaching. Classgrid is built around the real rhythm of academic life. A teacher can open the app, view today's schedule, enter a classroom, mark attendance, publish an assignment, share notes, review submissions, grade work, send feedback, and notify students without switching between disconnected tools.

For students, every teacher action becomes clarity. When attendance is recorded, students can see their standing. When work is assigned, students know what to submit. When grades are released, students receive the result. When learning material is shared, it reaches the right class. Classgrid keeps the teacher experience powerful, but not administrative-heavy. Teachers get the tools they need for teaching and evaluation, while sensitive institution controls remain with authorized administrators.

Classgrid for Teachers is the faculty workspace inside the larger Classgrid campus platform. It is designed for people who manage learning directly: school teachers, junior college lecturers, engineering professors, coaching tutors, mentors, and academic coordinators. The teacher experience is not a finance dashboard. It is not a principal dashboard. It is not a student app. It is a teaching command center. Teachers use Classgrid to manage their assigned academic responsibilities.
Classes:
view assigned classrooms, subjects, batches, divisions, or learning groups.
Attendance:
record student participation for the sessions they teach.
Assignments:
create work, collect submissions, grade responses, and share feedback.
Tests and quizzes:
run practice checks, internal assessments, and online evaluations where enabled.
Timetable:
follow schedule, classes, extra lectures, holidays, and academic planning.
Learning material:
publish notes, videos, references, announcements, and study resources.
Communication:
message students, send notifications, reply to class activity, and participate in forums.
Analytics:
understand class activity, learning engagement, and student progress where available.
Classgrid gives teachers a single place to run the academic day.

Classgrid supports different teaching roles because the work of a school teacher, junior college lecturer, engineering professor, and coaching tutor is not identical. The platform keeps the common teaching foundation consistent, while allowing the institution type to shape the experience.

For a school teacher, Classgrid focuses on daily discipline, homework, attendance, parent visibility, class communication, and student follow-up. School teachers often manage frequent homework, strict attendance, daily class routines, parent expectations, and student behavior patterns.
Homework and assignments:
teachers can publish work for their students and track submissions.
Strict attendance:
teachers can record daily or class-level attendance so absences are visible quickly.
Class notices:
announcements can reach the right student group without depending on physical diaries.
Parent visibility:
when the school enables parent communication, attendance and academic updates can support better home follow-up.
Student support:
teachers can identify who is missing work, absent often, or falling behind.
The school teacher experience is built for consistency and accountability.

For a junior college lecturer, Classgrid supports the transition from school-style structure to college-style independence. Junior college students are preparing for board exams, entrance tests, stream decisions, practicals, and future admissions. Lecturers need tools to keep them focused.
Stream-based teaching:
lecturers can manage students across Science, Commerce, Arts, or other streams offered by the institution.
Board exam preparation:
assignments, internal tests, timetable, results, and curriculum tracking support structured preparation.
CET and entrance practice:
quizzes and online exams can support competitive preparation where enabled.
Attendance awareness:
lecturers can help students avoid eligibility issues by keeping attendance visible.
Study continuity:
notes, announcements, feedback, and schedules keep students aligned throughout the year.
The junior college lecturer experience is built for high-pressure academic preparation.

For an engineering professor, Classgrid supports complex academic delivery: subject assignments, practicals, lab batches, internal assessments, credits, semester exams, and technical resources. Engineering teaching is layered. A professor may handle lectures, labs, tutorials, internal tests, project reviews, question preparation, grading, and result support.
Assigned subjects:
professors can see the classes and subjects connected to their teaching responsibility.
Practical work:
assignments and submissions can support lab records, practical files, and technical documentation where enabled.
Internal assessments:
tests, quizzes, marks, and grading support semester evaluation.
Technical notes:
professors can share PDFs, references, lecture material, and marketplace resources.
Exam support:
faculty can contribute to online exams, grading, and question workflows when authorized.
The engineering professor experience is built for depth and academic precision.

For a coaching tutor, Classgrid focuses on speed, practice, testing, notes, and performance feedback. Coaching students need frequent assessment and fast improvement. Tutors need to run many practice cycles without manual overload.
Test practice:
tutors can use quizzes, online exams, and internal tests for topic-wise and mock-exam preparation.
Fast feedback:
grading and result updates help students correct mistakes quickly.
Notes and packages:
tutors can share study material, question banks, and premium learning resources where enabled.
Batch communication:
tutors can notify students about tests, revisions, extra sessions, and assignments.
Performance focus:
analytics help tutors understand who needs help and where the batch is struggling.
The coaching tutor experience is built for measurable improvement.
A teacher in Classgrid may hold different academic responsibilities depending on how the institution assigns work. These responsibilities define what the teacher can see and manage.
Class Teacher:
responsible for a class, division, or group. This role often focuses on student coordination, class-level monitoring, attendance awareness, and communication.
Subject Teacher:
responsible for a specific subject in a class or division. This role focuses on teaching, assignments, subject attendance, tests, grading, and resources.
Assistant Teacher:
supports a subject or class under the institution's structure. This role may help with teaching, support, review, or coordination where allowed.
Mentor:
guides students academically or personally, especially in coaching, higher education, or structured mentoring programs.
Academic Coordinator:
may review progress across subjects, batches, or classes when assigned by the institution.
Exam Contributor:
may help create tests, evaluate work, or support grading when authorized by the examination workflow.
Classgrid keeps these responsibilities clear so teachers do not accidentally access areas outside their assigned work.

Teacher permissions are focused on assigned academic work. A teacher can manage the classes, subjects, batches, or groups connected to their role. They cannot automatically access every student, every fee record, every payroll item, or every administrative setting.
Can manage assigned academic activity:
classes, attendance, assignments, tests, quizzes, notes, grades, and feedback for assigned groups.
Can communicate with students:
announcements, messages, notifications, forum activity, and academic updates where enabled.
Can review submissions:
student work can be checked, graded, and returned with feedback.
Can support exams:
online exams, grading, internal tests, and question workflows are available where the institution authorizes them.
Cannot access private student records outside scope:
teachers do not receive unrestricted access to every student in the institution.
Cannot manage finance by default:
fee structures, defaulter lists, receipts, waivers, and institutional collection reports remain with fees staff unless the institution assigns extra authority.
Cannot manage payroll by default:
staff salaries, payslips, and HR payroll controls stay with authorized HR staff.
Cannot change institution settings by default:
organization setup, plans, billing, compliance settings, and platform controls remain with admins.
This gives teachers enough power to teach well, while protecting sensitive institutional operations.

The Teacher Dashboard is intentionally simple. Instead of filling the sidebar with every academic feature, Classgrid keeps the main navigation focused and places the detailed teaching tools inside the Work page. This keeps the teacher experience clean even when the institution uses many modules.
Core:
Home, Work, and Schedule.
Connect:
Messages, Notifications, and Forum.
Tools:
Classgrid AI, Google Drive, and Virtual ID.
Institution links:
Requests, What's New, Organization, Platform Feedback, and Marketplace.
User menu:
Profile, Settings, Help and Support, and Log out.
The teacher can quickly move between daily teaching, communication, tools, and account actions without navigating a heavy admin console.

My Class:
view assigned classrooms and student groups.
My Roles:
understand whether the teacher is assigned as class teacher, subject teacher, assistant, mentor, or another academic role.
Assignments:
create work, collect submissions, grade responses, and send feedback.
Internal Test:
manage internal assessment activity.
Academic Planning:
plan lessons, topics, progress, and academic delivery.
Curriculum:
connect teaching to the institution's learning structure.
Certificate:
view or support certificates where authorized.
Attendance:
record and review class participation.
Manage Leaves:
manage leave-related academic workflows where enabled.
Events:
participate in campus events and academic activities.
Result:
access result-related academic workflows where authorized.
Feedback:
collect or respond to structured feedback.
My Time Table:
view assigned teaching schedule.
Examination:
support exam activity where assigned.
Quiz Manager:
create and manage quizzes.
Holidays:
view institution holidays and plan teaching accordingly.
Go Live:
conduct live sessions where enabled.
Classgrid AI:
use AI-assisted study and teaching support where enabled.
Online Exam Builder:
build digital exams where authorized.
Exam Grading:
review and grade exam submissions where assigned.
Analytics:
review faculty and classroom performance insights.
Notes Marketplace:
share, review, or access learning material where enabled.
Canteen:
access campus canteen workflows where enabled.
Alumni:
participate in alumni or placement-connected activity where enabled.
Profile:
manage teacher profile and account details.
The Work Page makes the teacher experience complete without making everyday navigation messy.

Classrooms are the center of the teacher experience. A classroom connects a teacher to the right students, subject, learning material, assignments, announcements, quizzes, and activity. Teachers can use classrooms to organize academic delivery.
Create or manage class spaces where the institution allows teacher-led classrooms.
See students connected to the class or learning group.
Share announcements, notes, materials, links, and quiz activity.
Review student participation and classroom engagement.
Approve or manage student requests to join a class where that workflow is enabled.
Keep subject-specific communication separate from general campus messages.
For students, the classroom becomes a clear place to find work and updates. For teachers, it becomes the academic workspace for a specific learning group.

Join requests help teachers control who enters a classroom. When a student requests access to a class, the teacher can review the request and approve or reject it according to the institution's rules. This is useful when classes are shared by invite, when a student joins late, when a batch changes, or when classroom access needs teacher confirmation.
Teachers can see pending requests where enabled.
Approved students can access the classroom content and activity.
Rejected or pending students do not receive full class access.
Notifications can keep students informed about request decisions.
Join requests protect the class from becoming an uncontrolled group.
Attendance is one of the most frequent teacher actions in Classgrid. Teachers can record student participation for assigned classes or sessions, depending on the institution's attendance setup.
Daily attendance:
useful for schools and structured class environments.
Lecture-wise attendance:
useful for colleges and engineering programs where subject participation matters.
Batch attendance:
useful for coaching centers and practical groups.
Attendance trends:
teachers can identify students who are repeatedly absent or at risk.
Student visibility:
students can see their own attendance once recorded.
Admin visibility:
attendance summaries can help admins monitor class health and compliance.
Teachers cannot use attendance to manage institution-wide reports unless they have additional authority. Their focus is recording accurate participation for the students they teach.
Assignments help teachers turn learning into action. A teacher can assign work, collect student submissions, review responses, grade them, and return feedback. This creates a full academic loop.
The teacher publishes an assignment to the correct class or group.
Students view the assigned work in their app.
Students submit their own work before or after the expected deadline, depending on the institution's rules.
The teacher reviews submissions.
The teacher grades work and adds feedback.
The student receives the grade and feedback in their own experience.
Assignments reduce manual collection and make evaluation easier to track. They also give students a clear record of what was submitted, what is pending, and what has been reviewed.
Teachers can use quizzes, internal tests, and online exams to check learning regularly. This is useful across all institution types.
School teachers can run topic checks and homework-based questions.
Junior college lecturers can prepare students for board exams and entrance practice.
Engineering professors can run internal assessments, practical checks, and subject tests.
Coaching tutors can run MCQ practice, test series, and mock exams.
Classgrid helps teachers create a more consistent testing rhythm. Students get clearer practice and faster feedback.

Online Exam Builder and Exam Grading help teachers manage digital assessments where the institution enables those modules. These tools are especially valuable when assessments need to be conducted at scale or reviewed systematically.
Teachers can prepare digital exams where authorized.
Students can attempt assigned exams through their app.
Teachers can evaluate responses and release outcomes according to the institution's exam policy.
Exam teams can coordinate with faculty for grading and result readiness.
The institution remains in control of official exam publication. Teachers contribute to evaluation based on their assigned responsibility.

Academic Planning helps teachers move through the syllabus with intention. Instead of treating lesson delivery as a private notebook, Classgrid lets academic planning become visible to the institution where needed.
Teachers can plan topics, lessons, and preparation windows.
Departments can review whether teaching is moving on time.
Students benefit from clearer sequencing and less last-minute pressure.
Admins and HODs can understand syllabus progress without interrupting teachers repeatedly.
Academic planning is especially useful in board exam years, semester systems, entrance preparation, and compliance-heavy institutions.

Teachers can share notes, references, files, videos, links, announcements, and study resources with the right students. This keeps academic material organized around the class instead of scattered across informal channels.
Class materials:
teachers can share resources directly with the classroom.
Notes Marketplace:
teachers can participate in structured notes and study package workflows where enabled.
Recorded content:
where video learning is enabled, teachers can support students with recorded lessons or companion material.
Revision support:
teachers can share question banks, summaries, guides, or preparation files.
Student access:
students see material in their own learning workspace.
For teachers, this reduces repeated file sharing. For students, it creates a dependable study library.

Go Live helps teachers conduct live teaching sessions where the institution enables the module. This is useful for online classes, hybrid learning, doubt sessions, exam revision, coaching lectures, guest sessions, and emergency schedule changes.
Teachers can conduct live sessions for students.
Students can join from their own app experience where enabled.
Live sessions can support revision, explanations, and remote participation.
Recorded or companion learning material can support students after the session where enabled.
Go Live helps teachers extend learning beyond the physical classroom.

Classgrid AI helps teachers work faster and support students better where the institution enables it. AI can help with study support, note understanding, quiz preparation, content explanation, and learning assistance. It does not replace teachers.
Teachers can use AI assistance while preparing learning material.
Students can use AI support for revision and topic understanding where enabled.
Coaching and exam-oriented batches can benefit from faster practice generation.
Teachers remain responsible for judgment, accuracy, evaluation, and academic guidance.
Classgrid AI is a support layer, not a substitute for teaching.
Teacher actions can reach students instantly through the student experience. This is one of the biggest benefits of Classgrid.
When a teacher posts an assignment, students can see it in their work area.
When a teacher grades a submission, the student can receive the result and feedback.
When attendance is recorded, the student's attendance view updates.
When a quiz is published, eligible students can access it.
When notes are shared, students can open them from their learning workspace.
When an announcement is posted, students receive the relevant update.
This keeps the classroom synchronized without teachers needing to repeat the same information in multiple places.

Yes. Teachers can use Classgrid across desktop and mobile experiences. Desktop is useful for grading, planning, managing classroom material, reviewing submissions, and running heavier academic workflows. Mobile is useful for fast daily actions: checking schedule, sending messages, posting quick updates, viewing notifications, and handling classroom activity on the move.
Desktop:
best for deep teaching work and review.
Mobile:
best for quick action during the campus day.
Browser login:
teachers can use the web experience for full work sessions.
App login:
teachers can stay connected through the mobile app for frequent teaching updates.
Secure sessions:
Classgrid keeps teacher access protected while making everyday sign-in convenient.
The teacher experience is designed for both desk work and real campus movement.

The Teacher App and Student App are connected, but they are built for different responsibilities. Teachers create, manage, evaluate, and communicate. Students view, submit, attempt, respond, and track progress.
